contract: C4 (set_scopes), C10 (the allowlist line) and C11 (the relay's roots, the peer check), docs/protocol.md, since board ab-v16.30. The receiver (part 1a, board ab-v16.31) applies set_scopes, and the relay (part 2, boards ab-v16.35 and ab-v16.51) applies the allowlist line, by the same rules; both check their code against these vectors. Since board ab-v16.41 it also holds C5's sweep (the receiver, part 1a). Every value is a sample.
casesNote: in: the fields of a set_scopes request (or of an allowlist line). applies: what applies (lists, scopes, default and operator after the rules; a scope or list that applies as absent is not there). refused: the count in the answer. listOf: the list that a scope gets (null: no list), also for a scope that scopes does not name.

cases.note: The design's example (section 8.1): two lists, three scopes, no default.

A scope with null, or whose list is a valid name that is not in lists, has no list and never falls back to default; a scope that scopes does not name gets default. None of them counts. A value that is a string but not a valid name counts 1 and applies as null (the same count as for default and operator).
A default that is not in lists gives no list, with no count.
Entries that are not normalized are refused, 1 each; the other entries of the list apply.
A list whose name does not match the pattern, or whose value is not an array, applies as absent: 1, and 1 more for each entry of its array. A scope of such a list has no list.

A scope that does not match the pattern applies as absent and counts 1. A scope that matches it but whose value is neither a valid name nor null applies as null and counts 1: it has no list and never falls back to default.
A scopes that is not an object makes default apply as null: no scope gets the default list.
A default that is neither a valid name nor null counts 1 and applies as null.
A default that is a string but not a valid name counts 1 and applies as null, as the operator field does.
A missing default counts as one that is neither a valid name nor null.
A lists or scopes that is not an object applies as an empty object and counts 1.
A missing lists, scopes and default: 1 each.
An empty list applies: its scope is admitted and can open about:blank only; it has no scope rule (C5).
The operator field (choice 3): "*".
The operator field: a list name in lists.
The operator field: a valid name that is not in lists applies as null, with no count.
The operator field: null, as when it is absent.
The operator field: any other value counts 1 and applies as null (a string that does not match the pattern).
The operator field: a number counts 1 and applies as null.
The counts add up: a bad entry (1), a list that is not an array (1), a bad scope (1), a bad operator (1).

Names that are also properties of a JavaScript object (constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf) are names like any other; __proto__ does not match the pattern. A scope that scopes does not name gets default, also valueOf.
A list name that is a property of a JavaScript object, and no such list: a scope or default that names it has no list.

rawNote: A request as the bytes that the receiver parses.

raw.note: A name that comes twice in one object: the last one applies (JSON.parse and Python's json read it so). The daemon never sends one.

linesNote: The relay's allowlist line (C10, C11). peerCheck: the relay runs with --peer-check. roots: the roots map that applies (null: the peer check is off), or failClosed: true (the line applies no list).

lines.note: With the peer check: the roots map applies, a list for each scope.
With the peer check: a line with no roots field applies the lists, and no scope has a root (step 6 refuses each connection).
With the peer check: roots that is not an object applies as an empty object.
With the peer check: roots null applies as an empty object.
With the peer check: roots that is a string applies as an empty object.
With the peer check: an entry for a scope that does not match the pattern applies as absent.
With the peer check: an entry whose value is not a list applies as absent.

With the peer check: an item that is not an object with an integer pid from 2 to 2^53 - 1 and an integer start from 0 to 2^53 - 1 is dropped; the other items of its list apply, and other fields of an item are ignored. 9007199254740993 reads as 9007199254740992 in JavaScript, above the bound on both sides.
With the peer check: a scope whose items are all dropped has no root (step 6).
With the peer check: a scope that scopes does not name can have roots (they count for the defensive root rules).
With the peer check: scopes named like JavaScript object properties; __proto__ does not match the pattern.
Without the peer check: a line with a roots field (any value) applies no list, as if no line had come (the rootsWithout 503; open connections close).
Without the peer check: also roots null.
Without the peer check: also an empty roots.
Without the peer check: a line without roots applies as set_scopes does.
The relay ignores the operator field: a bad value changes nothing that it applies.

sweepNote: C5's sweep (board ab-v16.41). in: the fields of a set_scopes request. map: the receiver's tab-to-scope map before it (tab id -> scope; a tab of no scope is not in it: the operator's tabs, the restore tab, the about:blank of the window rule). applied: scopes and lists are objects (else no sweep, and the object is not the last applied set_scopes). orphans (optional): the tabs of the receiver's orphan set (tab id -> the old scope that it left, for the note only: the receiver keeps no scope for it), which are in no scope and not in the map; each applied sweep closes them, whatever their URL and whatever their old scope's list. noScope (optional): other tabs of no scope, which the sweep never closes. closes: the tabs that the sweep closes (their scope has no list, or they are in the orphan set), in tab id order.

sweep.note: A scope that scopes does not name, with default null: a session that ended (also while the link was down or no relay ran). Its tabs close, whatever their URL, about:blank too.
A scope named null (choice 5 b: an ended scope that never falls back to default): its tabs close; a scope that the object does not name has the default list, and its tabs stay.
A scope whose list is not in lists has no list: its tabs close (the relay closes its connections with 1008 already).
A scope that scopes does not name, with a default list (choice 5 b): it has the default list, and its tabs stay.
An empty list is a list: its tabs stay (they can open about:blank only).
A refused entry follows what applies: the value of md-bad is not a valid name, so it applies as null, has no list, and its tabs close. The daemon never sends one.
A list that applies as absent (its value is not an array): a scope that names it has no list, and its tabs close.
A missing default applies as null (C4): a scope that scopes does not name has no list, and its tabs close.

scopes is not an object: not an applied set_scopes, so no sweep. C4 applies it as an empty object, so every scope would have no list, and one bad message would close every agent tab; the tabs fail closed and stay.
lists is not an object: no sweep.
A missing scopes and lists: no sweep.

The orphan set (review-17d): tab 5 left scope md-old at an earlier sweep item that did not close it. md-old has a list again, but tab 5 is in no scope and not in the map, so the sweep closes it again, whatever its URL. Tab 3 is a plain tab of no scope (the operator's), and it stays.
No sweep at a set_scopes that is not applied: the orphan set stays too.
